priority: P1 — gap inventory G3. Numbers 0-20, the seven weekdays, the twelve months, today/date/hour and the age question are A0 staples that no shipped pack teaches. exam-a0 does not test any of them yet, so nothing is exam-blocked: this is a content prerequisite. Without these ids, any world line about an age, a date or a count has no bound options — the DEFECTS #14 phantom-decoy pattern.
why: Closes G3 in one pack instead of three thin ones: numbers 0-20 (21 ids), weekdays (7), months (12), plus hoy/fecha/hora/tienes/años. hoy is the teaches-word for Mateo 6:11, so the verse block binds to a real id in this pack. mañana already ships in unit-01 ('morning; tomorrow') and tengo already ships in a0-verbs, so neither is re-taught. hora also makes the ora/hora homophone pair both real pool words.
theme: Los números y el tiempo — numbers, the week, the year and how old I am
storyThread: Una semana en el pueblo: contar los panes, saber qué día es hoy, y decir cuántos años tengo

words.caption: Cero: no hay nada
words.note: cero = 0; no hay nada = there is nothing

words.say: Uno. Un pan en la mesa.
words.caption: Uno: un pan
words.note: uno becomes un before a masculine word: un pan

words.caption: Dos ojos, dos manos
words.note: dos is the same for masculine and feminine

words.caption: Cuatro sillas
words.note: cuatro (4) and catorce (14) look alike — listen for -torce

words.caption: Cinco panes
words.note: c sounds like s in Latin America, th in most of Spain

words.caption: Seis días de trabajo
words.note: seis rhymes with English «pace»

words.caption: Siete días
words.note: SYEH-teh: the ie runs together

words.caption: Ocho años
words.note: ch as in «church»: OH-cho

words.caption: Nueve horas
words.note: nueve (9) and nuevo (new) differ by one letter

words.caption: Diez dedos
words.note: the z sounds like s in Latin America

words.caption: Once panes
words.note: OHN-seh; nothing to do with the English «once»

words.caption: Doce meses
words.note: doce meses = twelve months = one year

words.caption: Trece días
words.note: TREH-seh: ce sounds like seh

words.caption: Catorce días
words.note: stress on -tor-: ca-TOR-seh

words.caption: Quince minutos
words.note: qu = k: KEEN-seh

words.caption: Dieciséis años
words.note: 16-19 are diez y + the number, written as one word; stress on -séis

words.caption: Casi dieciocho
words.note: diez y siete → diecisiete

words.caption: Dieciocho años
words.note: diez y ocho → dieciocho

words.caption: Casi veinte
words.note: diez y nueve → diecinueve

words.caption: Veinte años
words.note: VAIN-teh: one beat, no pause

words.caption: ¿Cuántos años tienes?
words.note: tener: yo tengo, tú tienes. ¿Cuántos años tienes? = How old are you?

words.caption: Tengo ocho años
words.note: año = year; ñ = ny as in «canyon»: AH-nyos

words.caption: Hoy es lunes
words.note: the Spanish week starts on lunes

words.caption: Mañana es martes
words.note: lunes and martes both end in -es and never change

words.caption: Pan el miércoles
words.note: the é carries the stress: mi-ÉR-co-les

words.caption: Hoy es jueves
words.note: j sounds like a strong English h: HWEH-ves

words.caption: Vamos el viernes
words.note: VIER-nes: two beats

words.caption: Jugamos el sábado
words.note: SÁ-ba-do: stress on the first syllable

words.caption: Oramos el domingo
words.note: domingo comes from the Latin for «the Lord's day»

words.caption: Hoy hay sol
words.note: h is silent: OY, as in «boy». hoy = today, mañana = tomorrow

words.caption: La fecha de hoy
words.note: la fecha = the date; hoy es lunes = today is Monday

words.caption: ¿Qué hora es?
words.note: h is silent: OH-rah — different from ora (he prays)

words.caption: Hace frío en enero
words.note: enero is the first month

words.caption: Frío en febrero
words.note: fe-BRE-ro: do not drop the first r

words.caption: Llueve en abril
words.note: stress on -bril: a-BRIL

words.caption: Flores en mayo
words.note: flores en mayo = flowers in May

words.caption: Sol en junio
words.note: j is a strong h: HOO-nyo

words.caption: Calor en julio
words.note: HOO-lyo: the i before o sounds like y

words.caption: Al río en agosto
words.note: g before o is hard, as in «go»: ah-GOS-toh

words.caption: Llueve en septiembre
words.note: also written setiembre in some countries

words.caption: Viento en octubre
words.note: ends like septiembre and diciembre: -bre

words.caption: Frío en noviembre
words.note: like septiembre, the i is barely heard

words.caption: Nieve en diciembre
words.note: diciembre is the last month

WAVE_NOTE: Wave themes: 1 = numbers 0-10 (render the numeral large with the word under it: es→numeral 0-10); 2 = numbers 11-20 then the age exchange (¿Cuántos años tienes? / Tengo ocho años); 3 = the week + date/time; 4 = the twelve months as one set (el año entero). This pack has NO TPR/sprite wave — every word is a hear-choose tile; 'diez dedos' is the one natural TPR action if a sprite wave is ever wanted. Waves 2 and 4 hold 12 words each (previous max 9): the game loop must paginate within a wave or split at render (DEFECTS #18). LEAD RULE 19:59: waves 1-4 + replay-5 as delivered.

scripture.verify: VERIFIED 2026-11-10 against RV1909 primary source (danielmiranda/rv1909hispano) — SCRIPTURE-rv1909-verified.md; corrects the RV1960 draft wording. teaches=hoy is a real id in THIS pack. The same verse ships in a0-u04 with teaches=pan: verses are not word ids, so there is no duplicate-id impact and both bindings are true. The only other verified verse, 1 Tes 5:17, teaches ora, which is not in this pack, so Mateo 6:11 is the correct choice.

QA.charset: ASCII + á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡ only in rendered fields; « » appear only in English notes and scripture.say (spoken-only)
QA.grammar: present tense only (es, hay, hace frío/calor, llueve, vamos, jugamos, oramos, tengo, tienes); no past, no subjunctive, no imperatives. Numbers, weekdays and months are nouns — no conjugation at all in this pack
QA.duplicateCheck: zero overlap with unit-01.json (52), a0-packs.json (49) and a0-verbs.json (30). Deliberately NOT re-taught: tengo (a0-verbs), mañana, día, noche (unit-01) — these appear only as option decoys and inside say/caption text
QA.optionsBoundToIds: every option string is a bound id in the union (verified by lead validation). No phantom decoys (DEFECTS #14). Decoy rule: adjacent number / adjacent month / adjacent weekday / minimal verb pair (tienes vs tengo vs está) / time-word pair (hoy vs ahora vs mañana)
QA.formIdRule: ids are the exact form the learner hears and the string on screen. The only new verb form is tienes (tener, tú) — tengo already ships in a0-verbs. años is an id because the age answer needs the noun (Tengo ocho años)
QA.numberIdDecision: 0-20 as 21 word ids, NOT '0-10 + teen pattern'. The pattern covers only 16-19, and those four still need their own ids for hear-choose validation; once-quince (11-15) are irregular and need ids regardless — the pattern shortcut saves exactly ONE id (veinte). Paying it buys: every spoken number is a real bound pool id, no grammar rule at A0 (audio-first mandate), numeral↔word mapping for ages/dates/prices
